title: Agent Failure Log Triage
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Analysis activity in which learners read six illustrative excerpts of an agent log and attribute each to one of six failure modes: Premature completion, Hallucinated result, Scope drift, Test weakening, Wrong arguments, or Runaway loop. Each excerpt gets one attempt in a fixed order, followed by the correct mode, the reason, and the mechanical defense for that mode. The run ends with a score out of 6 and a mastery statement at 5 of 6.

educational.topic: Recognizing agent failure modes in raw agent logs
learningObjectives: Differentiate six agent failure modes from six excerpts of an agent log, with at least 5 of 6 attributed correctly
prerequisites: The six agent failure modes: Premature completion, Hallucinated result, Scope drift, Test weakening, Wrong arguments, and Runaway loop

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; the drop-down and buttons are native HTML controls reachable with the Tab key, and the buttons respond to Enter or Space; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and check or X symbols as well as a blue or orange outline; log entries use a monospace font and notes use gray italics; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Choose a failure mode
controls.purpose: Chooses one of the six failure modes for the current excerpt. The choice can be changed until Submit is pressed. Disabled after submission.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Commits the chosen mode as the single attempt for the current excerpt. Enabled only after a mode is chosen.

controls.label: Next Excerpt / See Score
controls.purpose: Enabled after submission. Advances to the next excerpt, and after excerpt 6 shows the score summary.

controls.label: Start Over
controls.purpose: Shown on the summary screen; returns to excerpt 1 with no mode chosen.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Attribution of raw evidence to a named cause, with one attempt per case and immediate explanatory feedback naming the mechanical defense
keyQuestions: Did a tool actually produce the value the agent reported?
Was the check that defines success run?
Did the agent touch only what the request mentioned?
commonMisconceptions: A passing test run means the work is correct
An agent that touched extra files was being thorough
Repeated tool calls mean the agent is working hard
assessmentOpportunities: At least 5 of 6 excerpts attributed correctly on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Reading the definitions is exploration and is not evidence
